thread:
anna: heads-up: i've been thinking about a smaller-surface change: dual-path scoring for routing decisions. idea: policy gets two orthogonal scores -> operational_score (latency/health) and economic_score (cost/efficiency). saves us from jamming everything into one monolithic "score" number.
rick: nice. how would policy combine them? DSL-level math or a runtime combiner?

anna: preferred: keep it flexible. DSL can combine when owners want custom behavior, but provide a default combiner that normalizes ranges and yields a single composite score for simple policies.
marta: normalization is the tricky bit. tenants with small traffic have noisy economic numbers; that could skew decisions. need per-tenant z-score or percentile transforms.
sam: agree. propose we expose both raw and normalized variants: economic_raw, economic_norm. let the combiner use economic_norm by default.

infra-bot: reminder: any per-tenant state has storage/ops implications. estimate memory and checkpoint cadence.
rick: what about explainability? ops will want to know why a route was chosen. we should add a compact explain response from the decider: top contributing factors + deltas.

anna: yes. plan: GetDecision(route, tenant, hints) -> {path, composite_score, breakdown:["operational:0.73","economic_norm:0.22"], explain_id}. explain_id links to an on-demand trace with recent probe samples and normalization parameters. keep the inline payload tiny.
marta: that helps debugging. but we should cap retention for traces and make them tenant-scoped. also expose a sampling switch to collect more explains during canary.
sam: rollout idea: implement dual-path in simulator first. Run historic traces and compare route churn, p95 latency, and billing delta. If composite decisions increase hedging too often, tune default combiner.
rick: DSL change surface: add two helper funcs combine(op, eco, w_op, w_eco) and econ_norm(values, method="percentile"). Backwards compatible: old 'score' maps to composite_score for now.

anna: plus a lint rule: warn if policy directly references economic_raw without a normalization wrapper.

marta: edge-case: what if a tenant pins cost to zero (promo) or has custom budgets? combiner needs to respect tenant overrides while still preventing noisy oscillation. maybe add a budget-aware damping term.
sam: we could add confidence bands on each score, similar to probes. combiner can downweight low-confidence signals.

infra-bot: action required: add schema change request to decider API and do compatibility test with existing SDKs.
rick: logging/telemetry: emit histograms for op_score, econ_score, econ_norm, composite_score; also a churn metric for route flips per 10k requests.

anna: perf note: decider must compute these quickly. prefer doing normalization with streaming stats (approx quantiles) in memory rather than full window sorts.
marta: for simulation, i'll wire percentile-normalization and run against last 30 days. goal: see false-positive fallbacks and cost delta.
sam: i'll add combiner variants to sim harness and run grid search on weights + confidence thresholds.
rick: ops: gradual rollout plan? start with shadow decisions for 7 days, collect explain samples, then 1% roll, monitor churn and cost.

anna: security/permissions: explain traces must be accessible only to tenant owners + infra. add RBAC check.
marta: also document how tenants can opt-in/out or set custom weights. adding an enterprise knob for managed accounts.

infra-bot: checklist: API schema PR, sim results, lint PR, telemetry dashboard, RBAC gating. assign owners in RFC.

anna: i'll draft RFC with API sketch, sample DSL snippets, and the sim plan. aim to share tomorrow. please comment especially on normalization methods (z-score vs percentile) and sampling heuristics. :sparkles:
